claims.claim: Melting removes up to 40 percent of a rock’s mass during the fireball phase.
claims.episode_span: Analysis of 75 documented falls showed melting, not simple evaporation, removes up to 40 percent of a rock’s mass during the fireball phase at roughly 60 kilometers altitude.
claims.source_title: Meteors don't just burn up. What really happens is far more violent
claims.supporting_quote: According to the researchers, melting alone can ultimately remove as much as 40 percent of the original rock's mass.

claims.claim: Fragmentation begins at air pressures roughly one-fifth the compressive strength of recovered meteorites.
claims.episode_span: Fragmentation begins at air pressures roughly one-fifth the compressive strength of recovered meteorites, possibly because heating and prior space collisions weaken the material.
claims.source_title: Meteors don't just burn up. What really happens is far more violent
claims.supporting_quote: The researchers found that rocks can start fragmenting when the air pressure acting on their leading surfaces reaches only about one-fifth of the strength measured in meteorites recovered on Earth.
